reasoning: The load-path core survives and I measured it independently. On a real /draft mount the page issues `/api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_main` and gets a 200 whose gzipped content-length is 1,180,466 (≈11.95 MB decoded), and the only field the mount-time call site consumes is `data.sleeper.teams` — 46,792 bytes, 0.39% (frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:3932-3937, `cache: "no-store"`, then `const teams = data?.sleeper?.teams || []`). The backend already serves etag + `cache-control: private, max-age=30` on that route, so `no-store` does defeat a working 304 path. /draft measured ≈2.1x /rankings in both decoded and transferred bytes, which corroborates the author's 'roughly double every other page'. My first measurement pass appeared to refute the whole finding (total decoded 11.9 MB, no /api/data in the response log) — that was my own instrumentation artifact: Chrome evicts response bodies over its buffer, `resp.body()` throws 'Request content was evicted', and my handler was swallowing it. Header-level accounting recovered it. So the finding is not killed. Three things are overstated and one is simply wrong. (1) WRONG: 'All three /api/data call sites consume only data.sleeper.teams ... 0.39%'. Call site 2 — fetchSyncPreview at page.jsx:4201-4224 — consumes `data.playersArray` (`setAllPlayersArray(pa)`, page.jsx:4233), which is 6,673,553 of the 11,954,874 bytes and is the entire point of that fetch. Its waste is the duplicated legacy `players` dict (5,914,408 b), not 99.6% of the payload. Two of three call sites consume only teams, not three. (2) OVERSTATED: 'from three separate call sites' on page load. Measured: exactly ONE completed /api/data response per load. Call site 2 is click-gated ('Sync rookies'); call site 3 (page.jsx:4484-4487) is gated on `allPlayersArray` being set, i.e. post-sync, and uses `cache: "force-cache"`, not no-store. The claimUnderTest analogy to the prior '/draft calling it three times per page load' fix therefore does not transfer — the per-load count is 1. (3) OVERSTATED: the bare `/api/data` is attributed to 'a third call site'. It comes from call site 1 itself, whose URL expression is bare until `selectedLeagueKey` resolves; the bare request is superseded and never lands. (4) BLAST RADIUS: playersAffected 1092 is meaningless here — no player value is wrong; this is a payload-weight finding. Priority held at P1, not lowered: the surviving defect (1.18 MB gzipped / ~11.95 MB parsed, on mount, on the app's most time-critical page, to read 12 team names, with the backend's own ETag deliberately bypassed) is a genuine violation of this repo's stated performance rules. Rescoped for claim scope, not severity.

correctedBlastRadius.note: routesAffected recounted to 1: /api/data and /api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_main are the same route, and /api/dynasty-data?view=array is fetched by /rankings too — it is not part of the /draft-specific excess. playersAffected recounted to 0 (payload weight, not a value defect). The per-load excess is the single mount-time fetch: 1,180,466 b transferred / ~11,908,082 b decoded to obtain 46,792 b of team names.

whatWouldSettleIt: Point page.jsx:3930 at a narrow view (`/api/data?view=startup`, or serve sleeper.teams from /api/leagues, which /draft already fetches at 840 b) and drop `cache: "no-store"`; then re-run the header-level Playwright accounting above and /draft's transferred total should fall from ≈2.25 MB to ≈1.07 MB, matching /rankings. Note the measurement must read `content-length` from the response headers — `resp.body()` throws 'Request content was evicted' on this payload and silently under-reports by 11.9 MB, which is what nearly overturned this finding.
